A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conformal prediction-based machine unlearning study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet experiments, including unlearning comparisons, calibration sensitivity, distribution analyses, and framework evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds comparator results, training trajectories, and probability/loss distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The central forgetting objective changes from max(S - q_bar, -Delta) in v1 Equation 8 to max(q_bar - S, -Delta) in v2 Equation 9. This reverses its optimization direction, now encouraging true-label non-conformity scores above the exclusion threshold. The surrounding framework remains, but this is a substantive correction to its defining loss. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation or experimental runs changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet image classification under 10% and 50% random forgetting and class-wise forgetting. The added diagnostics use retained task coverage; language modeling and generative modeling appear only as future extensions.

E2.justification: v2 adds SFRon across the benchmark comparisons and removes Fisher Forgetting from the CIFAR-10 CR, MIACR, and mis-label comparisons, including their appendix tables. NegGrad+ is also newly included in the CIFAR-10 class-wise comparison, although it already appeared in other v1 experiments: compare v1 Table 11 with v2 Table 9.

E3.justification: Section 2.3.2 changes the recommended/default miscoverage rate from 0.1 to 0.05, changing the settings emphasized in the main comparisons. Both retain the full 0.05–0.20 sweep and the same reported calibration sample counts. Added diagnostics compare out-of-set versus misclassified subsets and track accuracy across epochs. Newly disclosed budgets for existing experiments do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds CPU-FT accuracy trajectories across epochs and loss weights in Figure 3, plus UA-versus-CR softmax and cross-entropy distributions for FT, RL, Salun, and SFRon in Figures 7–10. These supplement retained Grad-CAM, loss-weight, shadow-model, and non-conformity density analyses. The calibration-size plot drops the alpha = 0.1 curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent trials and appendix results as mean plus or minus standard deviation. Additional rows follow the same practice. Corrected parenthetical gaps to retraining are comparison results, not changes in uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds SFRon results, CIFAR-10 class-wise NegGrad+ results, and diagnostic findings, while removing FF entries. It also corrects Tiny ImageNet framework gaps: for RT at lambda = 0.2 and alpha = 0.05, CR remains 0.458 but its gap changes from 0.486 to 0.045 in v1 Table 16 versus v2 Table 14. Shared baseline measurements otherwise match; changed headline rankings largely reflect the alpha switch.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the loss derivation and associated condition from q_bar - S >= Delta to S - q_bar >= Delta, aligning the mathematics with true-label exclusion. CR and MIACR definitions remain unchanged. The explicit quantile equation in v2 restates an existing calculation; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain identifying UA/MIA shortcomings, proposing CR and MIACR, and improving forgetting through a conformal/C&W loss framework while preserving utility. The fake-unlearning and CPU terminology reframe these contributions. The abstract's 6.6% average UA improvement summarizes gains already reported in v1 Section 4.3.

C2.justification: v2 links the retraining-gap criterion to privacy and the limit-based criterion to bias removal, expands interpretation of distribution alignment, and adds image-classification and calibration-data limitations in Appendix D. It replaces the generic impact statement with specific privacy-verification claims. However, v1's explicit warning that exchangeability may fail is removed, although distribution-shift discussion remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies method-specific unlearning budgets, including FT's 20 CIFAR-10 epochs and 5 Tiny ImageNet epochs, and reports a Tesla V100-SXM2 GPU with 32 GB memory. Original-model settings and calibration counts are retained. These are primarily new disclosures; v1's explicit statement that methods use the same forgotten class is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SFRon, label-agnostic forgetting, and Tailor conformal-prediction references. It replaces the Kurmanji learned-databases citation with Towards Unbounded Machine Unlearning and removes Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Net. Salun's preprint-to-publication update concerns the same work. The broader positioning around prediction uncertainty remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, metric motivation, loss explanation, and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting around fake unlearning. v1's standalone Section 2.4 is incorporated into the experimental narrative, and the appendices gain a distribution-comparison subsection, limitations, and a rewritten impact statement. Terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one column, with extensive table redesign and relocation. v1 Tables 4 and 5 become a combined v2 Table 3 with separate conventional-metric columns; the Grad-CAM table becomes Figure 1. Existing density plots are retained and relocated, the calibration plot is restyled and reduced, and new trajectory/distribution figures are added.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an important defect: v1's defining loss and derivation encouraged the opposite direction from the stated forgetting goal, whereas v2 Equation 9 correctly encourages true-label exclusion. Corrected retraining gaps and newly disclosed unlearning budgets further improve correctness and reproducibility. Removing the exchangeability warning weakens qualification of the privacy interpretation, but the substantial improvement in the core method specification provides a clear net quality gain.
